claims.statement: The Pi SDK is consumed through a narrow PiSdkPort of five entry points — resolve the agent directory, build a resource loader, create a session manager, open a persisted session manager, create a session — imported dynamically only when no injected port is supplied, so unit tests run without credentials, a configured model or a terminal.

createEvidenceAgentSession initializes lazily on the first prompt or start, shares one in-flight start promise between concurrent callers, resets that promise after a failure so a retry is possible, and dispose unsubscribes, disposes the SDK session and clears listeners.

A session starts with four authored instruction sections — role, modeling red lines, operator selection, turn workflow — appended to Pi's own system prompt and with noSkills set, so no project or user directory is scanned for SKILL.md; the prompt names only tools the desktop registers and contains no skill, reference-directory or shell-command relic, and the desktop runtime passes neither a skill directory nor an instructions override.

Pi's event stream is projected onto exactly five plain desktop events (text delta, tool start, tool end, settled, error) and unknown SDK events are dropped, letting the renderer cap transcript text and model tool calls as an activity list without importing the SDK.

The orchestrator registers eleven agent tools — get_api_diff, sync_api_projection, run_sensors, apply_model_patch, get_canvas_selection, the clause and blueprint readings, and four fulfillment operators — and each operator resolves references against a freshly loaded document before submitting its generated commands through the same applyModelPatch handler.

apply_model_patch rejects a command without a string type before reaching the session, returns the applied command types on success, and converts a rejected patch into an isError tool result instead of throwing into Pi.

Agent patches are a correlated round trip: the main process sends them over IPC with a 15 second timer and resolves a failure immediately when the owning window is already destroyed, and the renderer decodes and dispatches them with one dispatchAll call labelled agent:<rationale>, so each agent patch is one undo step and a guard failure is answered as a failed result.

The desktop agent runtime resolves the model source and project directory from the project's source form, creates one session with a single extension factory on demand, and debounces background sensor runs so a burst of model edits produces one verdict.

Agent runtimes are keyed per project root, started single-flight, disposed when the owning WebContents is destroyed, and their streamed events and sensor reports are sent only while that sender is alive; the whole IPC registration is disposed on before-quit.

Tests assert that the renderer's patch verdict returns to the tool, that an operator refusal produces a readable error with no command batch, and that operators read the project tree before naming the root contract.

Streamed activity and sensor verdicts leave the main process on separate IPC channels: projected session events feed the renderer's conversation state, while sensor reports feed the status bar and diagnostics, and both publications are skipped when the owning WebContents is destroyed because the renderer only subscribes.

The desktop fills five of the seven EvidenceToolsHandlers slots and leaves the optional loadBaseDocument and refreshApi unset, so an in-app get_api_diff answers that no comparison baseline exists and sync_api_projection degrades to re-checking the current document without writing anything.

An applied agent patch is reviewed after the fact: usePatchReview diffs the before and after snapshots, marks added, removed and modified entities on the canvas, and only calls session.undo() while the patched document is still the one on screen, so a later edit makes the review non-revertable and the bar withdraws the undo.

annotate_contract_clauses and read_service_blueprint are pure reads that emit no patch, and an unparseable blueprint is answered as an error result carrying the parse reason instead of an empty draft.

The renderer publishes its current selection and reduced selected entity to the main process whenever the selection or graph changes, and the runtime stores that context and serves it back to get_canvas_selection, so selection-aware answers need no model round trip.

PromptDock is one composer for both directions: Command or Ctrl+Enter sends, Escape stops a streaming run, workshop-step and reverse-mode chips prefix the next message, and useAgentSession.submit chooses between prompt and steer from its own running flag.

createDebouncedSensorRuntime collapses a burst of edits into one run, defaults to an 800 ms delay, exposes schedule, flush, cancel and isPending, and routes failures to onError so a background check never surfaces as an unhandled rejection.

The session layer can open a persisted transcript through sessionFile instead of creating a new one, but the desktop IPC layer supplies neither sessionFile nor sessionDirectory, so an in-app turn always starts a fresh Pi transcript in Pi's default session directory.

The workflow section advances one of seven steps per turn and fixes reading before writing — get_canvas_selection, annotate_contract_clauses or read_service_blueprint first, then one minimal batch through apply_model_patch followed by run_sensors — an order the prompt spec pins.
